result.topic_en: Euler poses the problem of determining the residues of fourth powers modulo a prime P, and begins the solution using a primitive root, distinguishing the cases P = 4n+1 and P = 4n+3.
result.transcription:
PER NVMEROS PRIMOS. 125
Problema.
80. Si omnes poteſtates quartae per numerum quemcunque primum P diuidantur, inueſtigare indolem reſiduorum, quae inde naſcentur.
Solutio.
Poſita $a$ radice primitiua reſpectu diuiſoris P, vt $a^{P-1}$ ſit infima poteſtas vnitatem relinquens, ac reſidua quaeſita orientur quoque ex hac progreſſione geometrica $1, a^{4}, a^{8}, a^{12}, a^{16}$ etc. eousque continuanda, donec exponens per $P-1$ fiat diuiſibilis, quod ſi eueniat in exponente $4\lambda$, erit $\lambda$ multitudo reſiduorum.
I. Sit diuiſor primus $P=4n+1$, vt ſit $P-1=4n$; vnde vt $4\lambda$ per $4n$ diuidi queat, erit $\lambda=n$, hocque caſu reſidua quaeſita omnia ex hac progreſſione geometrica naſcentur
$1,\ a^{4},\ a^{8},\ a^{12} \ldots\ldots a^{4n-4}$
quorum multitudo eſt $n$.
II. Sit diuiſor primus $P=4n+3$, vt ſit $P-1=4n+2$; vnde ſumi debet $\lambda=2n+1$, et haec progreſſio geometrica
$1,\ a^{4},\ a^{8},\ a^{12} \ldots\ldots a^{8n}$
dabit omnia reſidua quaeſita; cum autem $a^{4n+2}$ vnitatem relinquat vti $a^{0}$, termini
$a^{4n+4},\ a^{4n+8},\ a^{4n+12}$ etc.
Q 3 eadem

items.quote: Si omnes poteſtates quartae per numerum quemcunque primum P diuidantur, inueſtigare indolem reſiduorum, quae inde naſcentur.
items.english: If all fourth powers are divided by any prime number P, to investigate the nature of the residues which arise from this.

items.quote: Sit diuiſor primus $P=4n+1$, vt ſit $P-1=4n$; vnde vt $4\lambda$ per $4n$ diuidi queat, erit $\lambda=n$, hocque caſu reſidua quaeſita omnia ex hac progreſſione geometrica naſcentur
items.english: Let the prime divisor be P = 4n+1, so that P−1 = 4n; hence, in order that 4λ be divisible by 4n, λ = n, and in this case all the required residues arise from this geometric progression 1, a^4, a^8, …, a^{4n−4}, whose number is n.

items.quote: Sit diuiſor primus $P=4n+3$, vt ſit $P-1=4n+2$; vnde ſumi debet $\lambda=2n+1$
items.english: Let the prime divisor be P = 4n+3, so that P−1 = 4n+2; hence λ must be taken as 2n+1, and the progression 1, a^4, a^8, …, a^{8n} will give all the required residues; and since a^{4n+2} leaves unity like a^0, the terms a^{4n+4}, a^{4n+8}, a^{4n+12}, etc. [continued on next page].
